history.summary: Chintpurni Devi Temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, at Chintpurni in Una district on a ridge of the Shivalik range along the Dharamshala-Hoshiarpur road (~3,200 ft). Legend: an ardent devotee, Bhagat Mai Dass, had a vision of a young girl (the goddess) directing him to a pindi (sacred stone) and instructing him to build a temple there; his descendants still serve as the temple's priests. The Shakti Peetha legend says Sati's body was cut into 51 pieces by Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra — CONFLICT in sources: most say Sati's feet fell here, others say her head. The goddess is Chhinnamastika (the severed-headed one), one of the ten Dasamahavidya goddesses; per the Markandeya Purana, Chandi severed her own head to feed the blood-thirst of her attendants Jaya and Vijaya. 'Chintpurni' means 'remover of worries'. Four Shiva temples are said to guard the shrine from four directions.

name: Chintpurni Devi Temple (Chhinnamastika Shakti Peeth)
town_description: Chintpurni is a small pilgrimage town in Amb tehsil of Una district, Himachal Pradesh, at about 3,200 feet elevation in the Shivalik hills. It exists essentially around the Shakti Peeth temple of Chintpurni Devi and serves large flows of devotees, especially during Navratri and the Shravan Astami fair. It lies on the Dharamshala-Hoshiarpur road, about 40 km from Una and 56 km from Kangra.
